0.value:
These find a piece of text and put another in its place.

THE NODES:

string_replace  replace the text wherever it appears, even inside a word
word_replace    replace it only where it is a WHOLE word

word_replace VERSUS string_replace:
string_replace matches anywhere, so replacing "cat" also hits "concatenate". word_replace matches only whole words, so it does not. For anything language-shaped, whole words is almost always what you want, and the everywhere version's surprises are the classic source of mangled output.

Both are case-sensitive: "cat" does not touch "Cat".

'find' IS A PATTERN, NOT PLAIN TEXT:
It is read as a regular expression, so some characters have special meanings. A full stop matches any character, "colou?r" matches both "color" and "colour", and "cat|dog" matches either word. To find one of . * + ? ( ) [ ] | \ ^ $ literally, put a backslash in front of it. An unmatched bracket is an error, and the node then sends nothing.

LISTS:
string_replace given a list replaces within each item that is text and leaves numbers alone; a list goes out. word_replace turns a list of words into one string, joined with spaces, before it starts; a string goes out.

A STRING THAT STARTS WITH 'find' OR 'replace':
Text arriving at 'string in' whose first word is 'find' or 'replace' is taken as a setting, not as text: "replace dog" sets the replace field to "dog" and nothing is sent. Handy from a message box, a surprise in running text.

If 'find' is empty the input is passed on unchanged.

SYNTAX:
string_replace <find> <replace>
word_replace <find> <replace>

EXAMPLE:
word_replace colour color

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

string in:
The text. Receiving it triggers the node.

find:
What to look for.

replace:
What to put in its place. Leave it empty to delete what was found.

OUTPUTS:

string out:
The result.

RELATED:
unescape_text and printable clean up text that arrived from somewhere else. replace and int_replace do the same job on lists and numbers rather than within a string - see the replace help patch.
dict_replace holds many substitutions at once.
